Content.1. Mentoring is most effective when it c: Primary focus: Clinical teaching and curriculum development (bedside instruction, small-group facilitation, assessment of learners). Secondary focus: Program development and quality improvement (designing a structured continuity clinic curriculum, implementing and measuring QI initiatives aligned with departmental priorities).
Content.2. Within each area, what specific guida: Teaching/curriculum: crafting measurable learning objectives, syllabus mapping to ACGME milestones, building interactive cases and simulation sessions, creating fair and reliable assessment rubrics, best practices for giving formative feedback, compiling a teaching portfolio, and strategies for education scholarship (IRB considerations for educational studies, selecting venues for publication). Program/QI: using logic models for program planning, stakeholder engagement and change management, basic budgeting for educational programs, PDSA cycles and dashboard development to track outcomes, negotiating for protected teaching time, balancing clinical duties with education leadership, and introductions to the Academy of Medical Educators and regional educator networks.
Content.3. Career development goals-What does th: 3 years: Serve as co-director for a resident rotation, launch and evaluate a new case-based curriculum, publish 2–3 peer-reviewed education studies, and lead a unit-level QI project that improves a key process metric. 5 years: Transition to Associate Program Director or Clerkship Director, secure an institutional or foundation education grant, present workshops at national meetings (e.g., AAMC, SGIM), mentor residents and fellows in education scholarship, and achieve promotion with recognition for educational excellence. 10 years: Become Program Director or Vice Chair for Education, attain regional/national reputation as an educator, sustain funded education initiatives with measurable learner and patient-care impact, lead multi-site curriculum collaborations, and develop a pipeline of junior educators who advance to independent roles.
